We are reconciling controls for our upcoming vendor assessment and need two things from Redwood: 1) confirmation on how you treat cloud provider SOC reports (AWS/GCP) — are those treated as "carve-out" subservice reports or are they included; and 2) a bridge letter (or equivalent) that covers the audit period 2025-06-01 through 2026-05-31 that explains any reliance on subservice org reports and whether any subprocessors changed in that window.

Specifically, our InfoSec team needs: 
- A short statement on which controls Redwood takes responsibility for (application/configuration) vs which controls are delegated to cloud subprocessors
- A list of subprocessors with the latest attestation type & coverage dates (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, etc.)
- Bridge letter or carve-out confirmation that covers the full audit period (or alternative evidence if a full-period bridge is not available)

Can you send an initial response by EOD Tuesday? If you already have a bridge letter template, attaching that would help speed review.

Thanks,

Marissa — attaching a first-pass packet. Quick summary below, full text in attachments.

Summary (short):
- Cloud providers (AWS, GCP) for our hosted inference are treated as subservice organizations and their SOC 2 reports are "carve-out" (we rely on provider controls for infrastructure/security controls but do not include provider test results in our own SOC report).
- Redwood is responsible for application-layer controls (access provisioning in Redwood Console, model routing policies, customer data handling). We take responsibility for configuration and operational controls within our service boundary.
- We are providing: redwood_bridge_letter_draft_v1.pdf (bridge letter language that states reliance on provider reports for infrastructure controls, lists audit period, and clarifies Redwood responsibility), subprocessor_inventory_20260510.csv (names, attestations, coverage dates), and an excerpt of the AWS 2025 SOC 2 report we referenced (aws_soc2_report_excerpt_2025.pdf).

Notes on coverage and timing:
- Provider SOC reports we rely on cover the following windows: AWS SOC 2 Type II (2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31), GCP SOC 2 Type II (2024-11-01 to 2026-04-30). Both are carve-outs which means Redwood relies on provider operational controls for infrastructure but separately asserts application control effectiveness in our report.
- There was one subprocessor onboarding (LogStore Inc.) on 2025-11-15; LogStore has an ISO 27001 cert (cert date: 2025-09-01) but no SOC 2. We flagged compensating controls in our bridge letter.

I recommend we: 1) send the bridge letter + inventory + provider report links to Acme, 2) offer a short Q/A call if they need confirmation on specific controls, and 3) if they require legal-signed attestation rather than a bridge letter, escalate to legal/finance for signature.

Attachments: redwood_bridge_letter_draft_v1.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_20260510.csv; aws_soc2_report_excerpt_2025.pdf

-rishi

Jared — thanks, great questions. Consolidated answers below and next steps. Attached: finalized redwood_bridge_letter_signed_for_acme.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_20260510.csv (final), aws_soc2_report_excerpt_2025.pdf (same excerpt), and LogStore_contract_summary.pdf (contract start/end and scope).

1) Audit period coverage: AWS and GCP latest Type II reports do not extend to 2026-05-31. We confirmed with infra that there were no material control changes in April–May 2026 relevant to the infrastructure controls relied upon in the attached bridge letter. Per standard practice, we are providing a signed bridge letter that: (a) states provider reports are carve-outs, (b) confirms no material control changes in the gap months, and (c) documents that Redwood completed a configuration review in June 2026 that validated the deployed control baselines (we can provide the configuration review executive summary on request). The signed bridge letter is attached and countersigned by our Trust team.

2) LogStore: Contract start date: 2025-11-15. LogStore was not part of Redwood's SOC testing during the prior year; instead we applied compensating logging retention and alerting controls owned by Redwood (listed in the bridge letter under "Compensating controls for non-SOC subprocessors"). In short: Redwood owns the compensating controls (retention and enhanced alerting) and LogStore is constrained to read-only ingestion of telemetry.

3) Compensating controls (excerpt):
- Centralized immutable log retention in Redwood-managed store (90 days min) — owned by Redwood
- Additional WAF rules and network egress filtering applied at the Redwood VPC level — owned by Redwood
- Weekly cross-checks of ingestion vs. index (automated) with alerting to oncall — owned by Redwood

Next steps:
- If Acme is satisfied with the signed bridge letter and the inventory CSV, we can provide a DocuSign copy for records.
- If Acme requires a provider-signed extension for April–May 2026, we will engage AWS/GCP but that will take additional time.

Let us know and we can open a short (30m) call to walk through the bridge letter.
